evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Missing entirely. Rep jumped to availability check ('We might have an availability tomorrow') without framing the time commitment, quote promise, or waiting for agreement.
evidence_quotes.discovery_basics: Address and zip obtained ('11812 blue creek drive, 76008'); pod count and truck mentioned ('we have one big and one small and we also have a budget twelve box truck'); moving day partially confirmed ('tomorrow morning'); no explicit name confirmation in opening, and no city-to-city probing (customer volunteered Denver to Fort Worth context, but rep did not ask).
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Never asked. Rep moved straight into availability and logistics without asking 'Other than price, what are your biggest concerns about this move?'
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Partial. Items mentioned: pods (big/small), truck, refrigerator, bed. Property type (two-story house mentioned by customer: 'two story house'), floor/stories (customer said 'two story'), rooms/walking distance/additional stops not probed. Special consideration about husband's age and mobility mentioned by customer, but rep did not systematically gather logistics.
evidence_quotes.packing_services_offered: No. Rep never asked 'Would you like us to pack your items into boxes for you?'
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: No. Rep never asked about typical box count or overflow considerations.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Partial. Rep gave a rate ('$1,194 per hour for two guys'), trip fee ('$150'), and minimum ('two and a half hours'), landing at '$6,350' — but no personalization to customer's specific situation (her concern about husband's mobility, the scope of three unloading items, etc.). The anchor is generic to a two-guy rate, not tailored.
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Partial. Trip fee ($150) and minimum (2.5 hours) disclosed. No mention of 15-minute increments, the 'not a guess' commitment, or overnight fees. No transparency upfront about how the estimate was built.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Not asked. Rep gave the price ('$6,350') and customer immediately said 'I love it. I love it. I want it.' Rep did not ask 'Does that feel fair?' and did not pause for hesitation.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: No. Two Promises were never covered, so there is no loop to close.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Not asked. Rep did not ask 'What's still concerning you about this move?' or any genuine concern check in Section 6.
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: No. Rep never asked 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?'
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Never. Rep never asked 'Would you like our help with your move?' Customer initiated booking ('I want it. No, you don't need to tell me no more... Book my name right now, please'). Rep responded to customer's request, not his own ask.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Partial. Name and email confirmed (Lynn Bernard, Lynn Bernard 45 @gmail.com). Date and time confirmed (tomorrow, 8:30–9:00 a.m.). Arrival window implied (8:30–9:00 a.m.). Crew size confirmed (two guys). Phone number NOT confirmed. Addresses: customer's address given (11812 blue creek drive, 76008); pick-up address (Denver location) NOT confirmed. Notes for crew about customer's concern (husband's mobility/age) NOT captured. Rep confirmed 'they're gonna give you a call once before they leave the office, which is about a half an hour away' but no crew briefing about the specific moving challenge.

top_strength: Jules quickly confirmed availability and a concrete time slot (8:30–9:00 a.m. tomorrow), immediately solving the customer's time-critical need and earning her enthusiastic buy-in before any friction could arise.
coaching_note: Skip the warmth and go back to structure: open with the quid pro quo (time + dependable quote promise), ask their agenda before giving a price, and close with 'Does that feel fair?' followed by silence — you earned the sale by reacting to hers, but the rubric call card exists to win the ones who need more guidance.
